source: ACGME Orthopaedic Surgery of the Spine Milestones 2.0

level_1: Obtains an appropriate medical history and performs a basic orthopaedic examination, with guidance
Develops a basic differential diagnosis pertinent to spinal conditions, with guidance
Independently interprets diagnostic testing for complex spinal conditions
level_2: Identifies diagnostic testing for common spinal conditions
Obtains a history of the condition or injury, performs an orthopaedic examination, and recognizes complex or high-risk spinal conditions
Independently develops a comprehensive differential diagnosis based on the history and physical examination finding
level_3: Develops a basic differential diagnosis pertinent to common orthopaedic conditions, with guidance
Orders and interprets diagnostic testing for complex spinal conditions, with guidance
Develops and publishes on new physical examination maneuver
level_4: Obtains a history of the condition or injury and performs an orthopaedic examination for common spinal conditions
Develops a comprehensive differential diagnosis based on the history and physical examination finding, with guidance
Develops a novel diagnostic technique or tool
level_5: Interprets diagnostic testing for spinal conditions, with guidance
Independently obtains a history of conditions or injuries and consistently performs complex examinations of spinal conditions

subcompetencies.name: Evaluation and Management of the Adult Orthopaedic Patient

level_1: Obtains a patient history, performs a physical examination, and develops a differential diagnosis for patients across clinical settings
Formulates and executes a stabilization plan for emergent conditions
Leads an orthopaedic team in the management of patients with complex conditions (e.g., unstable fractures in the setting of medical comorbidities)
level_2: Manages patients with straightforward conditions (e.g., stable compression fracture), with indirect supervision
Synthesizes a plan to manage healthy patients with straightforward conditions, including operative and non- operative options
Leads an orthopaedic team in the management of emergent conditions (e.g., polytrauma)
level_3: Recognizes and initiates work-up of emergent conditions (e.g., cauda equina syndrome)
Independently manages patients and adapts the management plan for a changing clinical situation (e.g., development of neurologic deficit)
Develops a clinical pathway or guideline for the management of patients based on demonstrated clinical expertise
level_4: Orders and interprets diagnostic testing and consultations based on patient evaluation
Triages management of multiple emergent conditions
Leads a multidisciplinary team in the management of patients with complex conditions
level_5: Manages patients with straightforward conditions (e.g., radiculopathy)
Synthesizes a comprehensive plan to manage patients with complex conditions and comorbidities

level_1: Prepares patients for procedures, including patient positioning and post-operative planning, and performs a posterior approach
Develops a plan for managing complex complications
level_2: Manages simple complications
Performs uncommon complex and revision procedures (e.g., revision TLIF) and common lateral approaches
level_3: Performs uncomplicated procedures (e.g., discectomy, simple laminectomy) and assists with anterior procedures
Develops a plan and implements treatment for complex complications
level_4: Identifies complex complications
Performs rare or high-risk procedures (e.g., 360- degree fusion)
level_5: Performs common complex procedures (e.g., multilevel degenerative spondyloses) and assists with a lateral approach
Adapts surgical techniques for complex situations

level_1: Prepares patients for lower cervical procedures, including patient positioning and post-operative planning, and performs a posterior approach
Performs common complex procedures (e.g., multilevel degenerative spondyloses, foraminotomy) and a primary anterior approach; prepares patients for upper cervical procedures
Adapts surgical techniques for complex situations
level_2: Manages simple complications
Develops a plan for managing complex complications
level_3: Performs uncomplicated procedures (e.g., simple anterior cervical discectomy and fusion
Performs upper cervical and revision procedures (e.g., revision ACDF) and an anterior revision approach
level_4: [ACDF], simple laminectomy) and assists with an anterior approach
Develops a plan and implements treatment for complex complications
level_5: Identifies complex complications
Performs rare or high-risk procedures (e.g., 360- degree fusion)

subcompetencies.name: Operative Management of Traumatic, Infectious, and Neoplastic Conditions

level_1: Characterizes or classifies a disorder and discusses indications/ application of reduction techniques, positions the patient, and performs posterior approaches
Develops a plan for managing complex complications and initiates complex coordinated care
level_2: Manages simple complications
Performs uncommon complex or revision procedures (transpedicular decompression, corpectomy and reconstruction)
level_3: Assists with common complex procedures (simple osteotomies, laminectomy, positional reduction, closed cervical reductions) and assists with anterior approaches
Develops a plan and implements treatment for complex complications
level_4: Identifies complex complications and coordinates effectively in the multidisciplinary team
Performs rare or high-risk procedures (circumferential fusion, three-column osteotomies)
level_5: Performs common complex procedures (laminectomy, open posterior reduction/ stabilization of an unstable spine)
Adapts surgical techniques for complex situations

subcompetencies.name: Deformity (scoliosis, coronal/sagittal deformity, isthmic spondylosis, proximal junctional kyphosis)

level_1: Prepares patients for procedures, including assessment of skeletal age and bone quality, patient positioning, and post-operative planning; performs a posterior approach
Develops a plan for managing complex complications
level_2: Manages simple complications
Performs pelvic fixation and uncommon complex procedures (e.g., pedicle osteotomies, revision transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion [TLIF], low grade spondylolistheses)
level_3: Assists with common complex procedures (e.g., simple osteotomies, laminectomies)
Develops a plan and implements treatment for complex complications
level_4: Identifies complex complications
Performs rare or high-risk procedures (e.g., vertebral column resections, high-grade isthmic spondylolistheses)
level_5: Performs common complex procedures (e.g., simple osteotomies), assists with uncommon complex procedures
Adapts surgical techniques for complex situations

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of basic spinal anatomy, including surgical approaches
Independently evaluates plain films, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequences, and computed tomography (CT) scans and discusses indications for other forms of imaging
Independently plans accommodative post- operative care, including bracing, post-operative therapy needs, and mobilization of social resources
level_2: Obtains and documents an appropriate social and medical history, including a standard neurologic exam, signs or symptoms of spinal cord dysfunction, and coexisting medical or social risks
Anticipates complications and presents a management plans based on review of complex or unusual patient anatomy
Appropriately requests advanced imaging and neurologic studies
level_3: Obtains and provides a basic interpretation of relevant imaging studies
Adapts the peri-operative plan for an existing patient risks (e.g., poor bone quality, opioid addiction, lack of social support)
Independently manages patients with complex or unusual anatomy or bone quality (e.g., osteogenesis imperfecta, ankylosing spondylitis)
level_4: Identifies applied surgical approach, including nerve root variations and upper cervical vascular structures
Identifies the role of post- operative imaging to assess healing, complications, and instrumentation failure
Independently analyzes advanced imaging and neurologic studies
level_5: Synthesizes and prioritizes a differential diagnosis and anticipates potential complications for complex spinal conditions
Routinely leads residents through surgical anatomy (e.g., anatomy course, operating room teaching)

level_1: Articulates a methodology for clinical reasoning
Integrates evidence- based information to inform diagnostic decision making for straightforward conditions
level_2: Identifies resources to direct clinical decisions
Efficiently synthesizes information and integrates reflection to make clinical decisions for complex conditions
level_3: Demonstrates clinical reasoning to determine treatment goals
Integrates evidence- based information to inform diagnostic decision making for complex conditions
level_4: Selects and prioritizes relevant resources based on the scenario to inform decisions
Incorporates clinical reasoning to improve care pathways
level_5: Synthesizes information to make clinical decisions for straightforward conditions

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events
Describes local quality improvement initiatives
Discloses patient safety events to patients and their families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of w to report patient safety events
Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and their families (simulated or actual)
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_4: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Participates in local quality improvement initiatives
Role models or guides others in the disclosure of patient safety events
level_5: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (simulated or actual)
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community level

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination
Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations
level_2: Identifies key elements for safe and effective transitions of care and hand-offs
Role models effective coordination of patient- centered care among multidisciplinary teams
level_3: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations effectively using the roles of interprofessional team members
Role models and advocates for safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs
level_4: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in straightforward clinical situations
Analyzes the process of care coordination and leads in the design and implementation of improvements
level_5: Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations effectively using the roles of interprofessional team members
Improves quality of transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Describes basic health payment systems, including government, private, public, and uninsured care, as well as different practice models
level_2: Describes how working within the health care system impacts patient care, including billing and coding
level_3: Analyzes how personal practice affects the system (e.g., length of stay, readmission rates, clinical efficiency)
level_4: Uses shared decision- making in patient care, taking into consideration costs for the patient
level_5: Participates in advocacy activities for health policy

level_1: Demonstrates how to access and use available evidence, and incorporate patient preferences and values to the care of a straightforward condition
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits patient preferences and values to guide evidence- based care
level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient preference, to the care of complex conditions
level_4: Critically appraises and applies evidence, even in the face of uncertainty and conflicting evidence, to guide care tailored to the individual patient
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex conditions and/or participates in the development of guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Accepts responsibility for personal and professional development by establishing goals
Creates and implements a learning plan to optimize educational and professional development
level_2: Identifies the strengths, deficiencies, and limitations in one’s knowledge and expertise
Actively seeks feedback and other input with adaptability and humility
level_3: Demonstrates openness to feedback and other input to inform goals
Uses ongoing reflection, feedback, and other input to measure the effectiveness of the learning plan and, when necessary, improves it
level_4: Analyzes and reflects on the strengths, deficiencies, and limitations in one’s knowledge and expertise to design a learning plan, with assistance
Role models consistently seeking feedback and other input with adaptability and humility
level_5: Responds to feedback and other input episodically, with adaptability and humility
Coaches others on reflective practice

level_1: Identifies and describes inciting events for professionalism lapses
Integrates ethical principles and recognizes the need to seek help in complex situations
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of the ethical principles underlying patient care (e.g., informed consent, surrogate decision making, advance directives, confidentiality, error disclosure, stewardship of limited resources, and related topics)
Recognizes situations that may promote professionalism lapses and intervenes to prevent lapses in oneself and others
level_3: Demonstrates insight into professional behavior in straightforward situations
Recognizes and uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas (e.g., ethics consultations, literature review, risk management/legal consultation)
level_4: Applies ethical principles in straightforward situations and takes responsibility for lapses
Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_5: Demonstrates professional behavior in complex situations
Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution

level_1: Reliably arrives to clinical activities on time and describes strategies for ensuring timely task completion
Proactively completes tasks and responsibilities to ensure that the needs of patients, teams, and systems are met
level_2: Responds promptly to requests or reminders to complete tasks and responsibilities
Recognizes barriers that may impact others’ ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_3: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in straightforward situations
Develops processes to enhance others’ ability to efficiently complete patient care tasks and responsibilities
level_4: Completes tasks and responsibilities without reminders
level_5: Prioritizes tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex situations

level_1: Recognizes the importance of addressing personal and professional well-being (e.g., physical and emotional health)
Independently develops a plan to promote personal and professional well-being
level_2: Lists available resources for personal and professional well-being
Describes institutional factors that positively and/or negatively affect well-being
level_3: Describes institutional resources that are meant to promote well-being
Creates institutional-level interventions that promote colleagues’ well-being
level_4: Discusses a plan to promote personal and professional well-being with institutional support
Describes institutional programs designed to examine systemic contributors to burnout
level_5: Recognizes which institutional factors affect well-being

level_1: Demonstrates respect and establishes rapport with patients and patients’ families (e.g., situational awareness of language, disability, health literacy level, cultural differences)
Answers questions about straightforward treatment plans, with assistance
Recognizes biases and integrates the patient’s viewpoint and autonomy to ensure effective communication
level_2: Communicates with patients and their families in an understandable and respectful manner
Establishes a therapeutic relationship in challenging encounters (e.g., shared decision making)
Counsels patients through the decision- making process for complex conditions
level_3: Demonstrates basic understanding of the informed consent process
When prompted, reflects on biases while attempting to minimize communication barriers
Coaches others in the facilitation of difficult conversations
level_4: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in straightforward encounters
Counsels patients through the decision-making process for straightforward conditions
Guides others in situational awareness and critical self-reflection
level_5: Identifies barriers to effective communication (e.g., health literacy, cultural differences)
Facilitates difficult discussions with patients and their families, (e.g., explaining complications, therapeutic uncertainty)
Counsels patients through the decision-making process for uncommon conditions

level_1: Recognizes the value and role of each team member and respectfully interacts with all members of health care team
level_2: Communicates in a professional and productive manner to facilitate teamwork (e.g., active listening, updates in timely fashion)
level_3: Actively recognizes and mitigates communication barriers and biases with health care team members
level_4: Facilitates respectful communications and conflict resolution with the multidisciplinary health care team
level_5: Is an exemplar of effective and respectful communication strategies

level_1: Accurately records information in the patient record while safeguarding patient personal health information
Independently communicates via written or verbal methods based on urgency and context
level_2: Demonstrates accurate, timely, and efficient use of the electronic health record to communicate with the health care team
Uses appropriate channels to offer clear and constructive suggestions to improve the system
level_3: Uses appropriate communication methods (e.g., face-to-face, voice, electronic)
Facilitates improved written and verbal communication of others
level_4: Concisely reports diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning while incorporating relevant outside data
Guides departmental or institutional communication around policies and procedures
level_5: Respectfully initiates communications about concerns in the system
